title: Give your coding agent a project memory and done-checks
summary: A developer built a three-language website with Claude Code, using a wiki, lesson rules turned into tests, and screenshot checks before the agent may call work done.
agent_role: Claude Code researched, built and checked each site section, took and reviewed its own screenshots, and ran fact-check subagents; the author corrected mistakes, picked designs and reviewed results.
outcome: Author reports the setup let him request all remaining sections in one evening and review real pages the next morning; a fact-check subagent verified 12 claims in under a minute.
what_they_did: Mateusz Muszarski built his multilingual website with Claude Code. He kept a 33-page project wiki and a lessons file, fed to the agent by hooks at every prompt and after memory resets. Every correction became a rule, and rules that slipped became tests. Done meant passing checks plus screenshots the agent had to open.
how_it_went: He says he could ask for every remaining section in one go and review real pages the next morning. A subagent checked 12 claims in under a minute. He reports catching bugs that never threw errors, like an animation that silently didn't run.
worth_knowing: A build piped through another command reported success while its log said it failed. Read the actual output, not the agent's summary, or turn on pipefail.
prompt: Help me set up memory and done-checks for my project at [repo]. Create a short project guide that points to wiki pages by topic, and a lessons file where each correction I give becomes a one-line dated rule. Before calling any task done, run type checks, tests and [other checks], then take screenshots at phone and desktop widths in [languages] and look at them yourself. When facts are missing, insert a searchable placeholder instead of inventing them. Show me the proposed setup files before writing them.

curation.rationale: Detailed, real-project walkthrough of memory, checks and screenshot review with Claude Code; useful and reproducible, though the theme overlaps other proof-before-done setups.
